key_insight: Personalized generation benefits from test-time alignment, where a small factorized ranking model can efficiently select better outputs from large candidate pools.
engineering_relevance: A million-parameter ranker reused from the base LLM’s embeddings provides a practical, low-latency alternative to billion-parameter reward models for scalable personalized inference.
method: Analyze personalized generation as a candidate-matching problem suited to Best-of-N test-time scaling.
Train a parameter-efficient MLP ranking model on fine-grained personalization data using internal embeddings from the base generator.
Use the ranker to score large candidate pools and guide selection without materializing expensive heavyweight reward models.
evidence_signal: Across nine datasets spanning three personalized generation settings, the method outperformed billion-parameter generalist reward models on every dataset, with under 0.4% of their parameters and four orders of magnitude lower scoring latency.
watch_item: Results depend on high-quality personalized preference data and the approach still requires generating multiple candidates at test time, so candidate generation cost remains a practical consideration.
paper_title: Rethinking Personalized Generation: Test-Time Alignment via Factorized Ranking Models
